hook: Move a real camera over a city block: lift your eye from the sidewalk to a helicopter, turn, change lenses and tilt, and watch the horizon and the two vanishing points follow. Then ink your own skyline over guides that obey the same rules.
outcome: Set up two- and three-point perspective from eye height, viewing angle and lens, and draw, hatch, fill and refine a city drawing that follows it
sources: NCAS Visual Arts VA:Cr2, VA:Cr3: https://www.nationalartsstandards.org/
Joseph D'Amelio, Perspective Drawing Handbook (Dover, 2004): horizon at eye level, two-point construction, the 90 degree angle between the sight lines, three-point when the picture plane tilts
Richard Szeliski, Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications, 2nd ed. (2022), section 2.1: https://szeliski.org/Book/
Settings, not facts: 3.5 m per floor, the lot grid, the example city and the eye standing back 6 m per meter of height
City, sky, guides and plan drawn in code
